quotes.text: “SB24-205 is a significant step towards ensuring that AI systems are developed and deployed in ways that respect individual rights, promote fairness, and shed some much-needed light on the ways companies are using AI systems to make key decisions about our lives.” -@AlexReeveGivens from @CenDemTech

“This law ensures that AI technologies are used in a manner that is transparent, fair, and accountable, protecting consumers and fostering trust in these powerful tools.” -@pweiser https://t.co/H7tWkwxNt3

“By setting high standards for AI accountability and transparency, we are not only protecting consumers but also fostering an environment of trust and innovation in our state.” -@BriannaForCO https://t.co/H7tWkwxNt3

You can see the full Press Release about the Colorado AI Consumer Protection Bill here:

https://t.co/Ds5yyN4XN6

It outlines the important steps we’re taking to protect consumers from discriminatory algorithms while ensuring our AI systems continue to grow sustainably.

We just passed the most far-reaching AI law in the nation!

Colorado’s new law will protect workers, tenants, and consumers from discriminatory algorithms that perpetuate the racism, sexism, and ableism of our past.

Here’s our Press Release: https://t.co/QJ6JmJo0SP

We passed the most far-reaching AI law in the nation!👨🏽‍💻

We must make technology work for everyone, not just a privileged few.

SB24-205 will protect workers, tenants, and consumers from discriminatory algorithms that perpetuate the racism, sexism, and ableism of our past. https://t.co/Dslc9P97Zk
We still have a lot to do. But I think this is a great first step, a really significant and robust first step to make sure that technology works for everyone, not just a privileged few.
This bill is about ensuring that when AI developers see real safety threats emerging from their work, they can report those concerns without fear of retaliation.

If a whistleblower at a large AI company realizes that their model could be misused for bioterrorism, they should be able to report it to their company or state or federal authorities without retaliation.

Congress needs to make sure artificial intelligence works for people and not the other way around. Giant corporations are putting profits ahead of people, pushing reckless experiments that risk global catastrophe for our family’s health, our kids’ future, and our paychecks. Nobody voted for this.
I have passed laws and co-sponsored laws that make sure that we protect Colorado's consumers and workers, while creating a reasonable floor that all businesses have to abide by.

Trump is attacking my efforts that created safeguards for AI because I stand in the way of Trump and Musk's plot to enrich themselves. 

Coloradans deserve technology that works for everyone, not just billionaires. https://t.co/zZKB2bqCnJ

I’ve delivered on my promise to protect Coloradans from the risks of AI, passing common-sense laws that Gabe Evans opposed. I understand that important decisions around your family’s healthcare, your hard-earned job, and your fundamental rights should be decided by people, not harmful algorithms or powerful corporations.

AI can, of course, deliver real benefits. I will work tirelessly and use my experience and insights to make sure artificial intelligence works for people, not the
other way around.

(4/4)
I will also work to fund cyber defense for hospitals, water, and the grid against AI-enabled attacks. I also support age checks and parental controls on AI chatbots for minors, to keep kids safe online.

(3/4) 
(1) requiring large AI firms to report critical safety incidents in a timely manner 
(2) requiring independent safety reviews before major model releases 
(3) implementing protections for whistleblowers 
(4) holding AI firms that lie to the government about safety practices or infringe on privacy rights accountable 
(5) requiring notice before AI-driven layoffs at large employers

(2/4)
Families deserve strong protections, real accountability, and a fair shot. That's why I support policies that ensure AI companies are not above the law. 

That includes:

I’ve been thinking about the risks of AI for years, which is why I passed the first comprehensive AI bill in the country back in 2024 in the Colorado State House. It got bipartisan support.

We also got bipartisan support for my bill allowing whistleblowers at AI companies to come forward with catastrophic risks.

Bigger action is long overdue. 🧵

Tens of thousands of incidents of increasingly-powerful AI agents going rogue.

These AI companies are racing without guardrails towards powerful models that could put our families at risk and lead us to an existential crisis. 

Congress must act. Now. 
https://t.co/vPsI3ke6OX

Researchers building AI are telling us the risks could be existential. 

Others say we should just “accept some bad things happening.” 

Congress needs to set guardrails before any catastrophic harms happen, not after.
https://t.co/77IO4eB8zd

What did Gabe Evans do to address the catastrophic risks of AI?

Worse than nothing. Time and time again, he has tried to preempt states' rights and undermine common-sense safeguards.

Coloradans will have their say in November. His days in Congress are numbered. https://t.co/EDAy8mxtLb

It’s un-American, it is unpatriotic what’s happening right now. We are just allowing corporate executives to dictate the future of humanity.
